what_is_enforced: The declared class SUBTRACTS. evaluate_claim_transition calls evaluate_claim_transition_substrate first and returns early on anything but Grant, so a class can refuse a claim the substrate would grant and can never grant one the substrate refuses.

Ambiguity blocks retry. A reconciliation_required prior with no reconciliation refuses checkpointable, reconciliation_required and non_retryable by name, sends compensatable to CompensateFirst, and admits only replayable, whose exact replay changes nothing either way.

Restore never reconciles. effect_is_reconciled requires reconciliation.source == external_system_readback AND an outcome of effect_landed or effect_did_not_land; a restored environment, a restored backup or a re-read local record satisfies neither.
Restart reconciles rather than re-invokes. A claim stamped with a dead incarnation becomes ReconcileOrphanedClaim, and the drill proves the check sees it if that turns into a Grant.

One member set. RecoveryClass is closed over exactly the ontology action contract's frozen EFFECT_RECOVERY_CLASSES, which is exactly canon's list; the drill widens the frozen list on one side and requires red.
findings: A RED THIS PROGRAM LEFT ON MASTER, found and fixed here. Commit c80621ac2 (M08.13/M08.14) added two MCP-bearing routes and classified both in MCP_ROUTE_CLASSIFICATIONS, which was necessary for the daemon to reach readiness — but a separate pinned COUNT test asserted the map held exactly 36 entries, and that pin was not moved. The unit's own verifier (check:standing-consumer-loop, 34/34) and the alpha journey were both green, because neither runs the daemon's whole suite; CI's `cargo test -p ioi-node --bin hypervisor-daemon` step would have failed. Re-pinned 36 → 38 with the two routes named in the comment. LESSON, the same one leg 1 recorded: a unit's own green verifier does not prove the estate is green — run the suite the pin lives in before claiming a cut landed.

SECOND VOCABULARY ON A CANONICAL FIELD (not fixed here — M04.6's owner): crates/services/src/agentic/runtime/kernel/runtime_work_lifecycle_log.rs, added by 704c4d0dd on 2026-08-25, matches the field named effect_recovery_class against none | reversible | compensatable | irreversible | ambiguous, and refuses anything else as work_lifecycle_cancellation_recovery_class_invalid. Canon's member set for that field is replayable | checkpointable | compensatable | reconciliation_required | non_retryable. Only compensatable is common to both, so a WorkRun child carrying the canonical class reconciliation_required is refused by the cancellation planner as invalid, and one carrying irreversible would be refused by the ontology action contract. Closure test: one member set for one field name, with a pinned test asserting the lifecycle planner's arms are exactly EFFECT_RECOVERY_CLASSES; recorded as R-16.

The unit's title says 'every action declares its recovery class'. What is enforced is that a DECLARED class is typed and honoured. No producer is yet required to declare one, and an admission with no class keeps the substrate's decision; making the declaration mandatory would refuse every existing effect path and is a separate, wider cut.
nonclaims: Pure claim-gate proof: no live external system, no provider call, no clock.
backup/restore as a whole remains check:backup-restore; this unit claims only that a restore does not satisfy reconciliation.
